questions.q: Allyl alcohol, CH₂=CH–CH₂OH, is stirred with activated MnO₂. The product is:
questions.explain: Activated MnO₂ oxidises the allylic alcohol only to the aldehyde and leaves the C=C untouched; it does not go on to the carboxylic acid.

questions.q: Hex-2-ene-1,6-diol, HO–CH₂–CH₂–CH₂–CH=CH–CH₂–OH, is treated with activated MnO₂. Which product is expected?
questions.explain: Only the allylic CH₂OH, whose C–H bond is weakened by the neighbouring π system, is oxidised; the saturated CH₂OH at the other end survives, and oxidation stops at the aldehyde.

questions.q: Which statement correctly contrasts SeO₂ and MnO₂?
options: Both oxidise saturated primary alcohols to aldehydes
MnO₂ puts an OH at the allylic carbon of an alkene, while SeO₂ oxidises allylic alcohols
SeO₂ cleaves C=C bonds, while MnO₂ forms epoxides
SeO₂ puts an OH at the allylic carbon of an alkene, while MnO₂ oxidises an existing allylic OH to C=O
questions.explain: SeO₂ makes allylic alcohols from alkenes and MnO₂ converts an existing allylic OH into C=O; used one after the other they can turn an alkene into an α,β-unsaturated carbonyl compound.

questions.q: Which alcohol is treated as unaffected by activated MnO₂ under the usual mild conditions?
questions.explain: Cyclohexanol is an ordinary saturated 2° alcohol and reacts very slowly. Benzylic and allylic alcohols, including cinnamyl alcohol and but-3-en-2-ol, are oxidised readily.
